pr_title: ddl: fix the set's  default value where `create table`
pr_body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to TiDB! Please read TiDB's [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/pingcap/community/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document **BEFORE** filing this PR.
-->

### What problem does this PR solve? <!--add issue link with summary if exists-->

- Fix #12160. Fix the issue when the set type default value is int type. 

- Fix an issue where the default value does not exist in the set.

### What is changed and how it works?

- Call `ParseSetValue` when the set type default value is int type. Mysql implementation also has problems, as follows:

```
mysql> create table t_set (a int, b set('1', '5') default 1);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.02 sec)
mysql> create table t (a int, b set('1', '5') default 2);
ERROR 1067 (42000): Invalid default value for 'b'
mysql> create table t (a int, b set('4', '5') default 1);
```
So code implementation reference [MySQL set type](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/set.html).

- Check if the default value exists in the set.

issue_context.title: SET type has inconsistent behavior compared with MySQL
comments: I suspect something is wrong against the filling the default value.

With the the following schema 
```
create table myset4(i int, s set('104','105','106') default 4);
```

TiDB's behavior:
```
mysql> create table myset4(i int, s set('104','105','106') default 4);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.14 sec)
mysql> insert into myset4(i) values(1);
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.04 sec)

mysql> select * from myset4;
+------+------+
| i    | s    |
+------+------+
|    1 | 106  |
+------+------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

MySQL's behavior:
```
mysql> create table myset4(i int, s set('104','105','106') default 4);
ERROR 1067 (42000): Invalid default value for 's'
```

review_comments: Should we attach the desc of SET type for a reference?
